properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:27PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A strong front moves toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight
tonight. Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled with
a lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2 feet
above normal high tide late tonight into early Thursday morning.
Strongest winds are expected to peak Thursday morning, with up to
0.5 inches of rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are
perpendicular to the southerly wind direction, such as
Kwigillingok, have a higher chance of seeing impacts with this
front. Strong southerly winds will continue through Thursday
afternoon and evening before slowly diminishing through Thursday
night.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 2:13PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...A warm front associated with strong Bering Sea low will
move into Western Alaska Wednesday evening into Thursday, with
widespread rain and gusty winds expected. Water levels late
Thursday through Saturday morning could rise 1 to 2 feet above
the normal high tide line along the Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...Late Thursday September 3 through Saturday September 5.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. Heavy rain and
gusty winds could make travel difficult at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels are expected to peak late
Thursday into early Friday and again Saturday morning. Gusty
east/southeast winds Wednesday night will shift to the
south/southwest Thursday into Friday, leading to more onshore
flow and the potential for higher water levels. Strongest wind
gusts across the West Coast will peak on Thursday around 30 to
50 mph, with around 0.50 to 1.25 inches of rain expected through
Thursday night. Winds will be lighter Friday and Saturday, but
will remain onshore.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 2 at 3:26PM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for Thursday. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 2:41PM CDT until September 6 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Shreveport LA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Shreveport has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River Near Diboll affecting Trinity, Angelina and Polk
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Diboll...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River near Diboll.

* WHEN...From late tonight to Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs.  Expect
flooded boat ramps and trails. At 14.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding
of boat ramps, paths, and trails.  Move livestock and equipment to
higher ground.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:15 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 1.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 14.7 feet early Friday
morning. It will then fall below flood stage early Sunday
morning.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Do not drive cars through flooded areas. Caution is urged when
walking near riverbanks. Turn around, don't drown when encountering
flooded roads. Most flood deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

For more hydrologic information, copy and paste the following website
address into your favorite web browser URL bar:
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/SHV

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 245 PM CDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM LATE TONIGHT TO SUNDAY EVENING

properties.description:
An Orange air quality forecast means that maximum ozone
concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 2 at 12:24PM CDT until September 2 at 9:30PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Hardin County in southeastern Texas...
Central Jasper County in southeastern Texas...
Northwestern Jefferson County in southeastern Texas...
Tyler County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 930 PM CDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1222 PM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to Heavy rainfall has occurred last night and this
morning. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 4 and 20 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lumberton, Silsbee, Woodville, Kountze, Sour Lake, Colmesneil,
Chester, Warren, Wildwood, Fred, Thicket, Saratoga, Town Bluff,
Rockland, Bevil Oaks, Village Mills, Honey Island, Caney Head and
Spurger.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.description:

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Texas, including the following
areas, Brazos, Coastal Harris, Grimes, Houston, Inland Harris,
Madison, Montgomery, Northern Liberty, Polk, San Jacinto, Southern
Liberty, Trinity, Walker and Waller.

* WHEN...Through Thursday morning.

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

- A swath of 3 to 10 inches has fallen over portions of southeast
Texas over the last 24 hours. Pockets of higher totals between
10-15+ inches has been observed in Liberty and Polk counties. The
remnants of Edouard have stalled over the Piney Woods which will
lead to additional periods of moderate to heavy rainfall through
Thursday. An additional 2-6 inches with isolated higher totals of
10-12 inches are possible over the next 24 hours. The NWS has
issued a High Risk for excessive rainfall and potential flash
flooding for the hardest hit areas especially as rainfall rates
will exceed 2-4 inches per hour. Those living in areas prone to
flooding should be prepared to take action should flooding
develop. Stay weather aware and be ready to take action when
Flash Flood Warnings are issued, particularly wireless emergency
alert Flash Flood Warnings for considerable and/or catastrophic
flooding.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 2 at 10:03AM EDT until September 2 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Detroit/Pontiac MI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 100 expected.

* WHERE...Lenawee, Livingston, Macomb, Monroe, Oakland, Washtenaw,
and Wayne Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.areaDesc: Pima, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 2 at 6:46AM MST until September 2 at 6:45PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by runoff from
previous days' rain. The Vamori Wash at Kom Vo is at 9.51 ft, which
is action stage.

* WHERE...Southwestern Pima County in southeastern Arizona,
specifically the Vamori Wash.

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Water may be approaching the bottom of the Highway 21
Bridge that goes over the Vamori.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 641 AM MST, gauge reports indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Hali Murk Wash, Vamori Wash, San Luis Wash, Gu Vo Wash, Gu Oidak
Wash, San Simon Wash and Sells Wash.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Santa Cruz and Kupk.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 645 PM MST THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 2 at 5:44AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A strong front moves toward the Kuskokwim Delta coast overnight
tonight. Southerly onshore winds gusting up to 40 mph coupled
with a lengthy fetch will promote elevated water levels 1 to 2
feet above normal high tide late tonight into early Thursday
morning. Strongest winds are expected to peak Thursday morning,
with up to 0.5 inches of rainfall. Areas of the coastline that are
perpendicular to the southerly wind direction, such as
Kwigillingok, have a higher chance of seeing impacts with this
front. Strong southerly winds will continue through Thursday
afternoon and evening before slowly diminishing through Thursday
night.

NWSheadline: ELEVATED WATER LEVELS LATE TONIGHT THROUGH THURSDAY MORNING FOR THE KUSKOKWIM DELTA COAST

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued September 2 at 3:03AM EDT until September 3 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...The Volusia and Northern Brevard Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A Moderate risk of rip currents continues
at the Treasure Coast and Southern Brevard beaches.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 1 at 2:37PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
The Mid-America Regional Council has issued a code Orange Air
Quality Alert for the Kansas City metropolitan area, with ground
level ozone being the primary pollutant until 7 PM CDT this evening.
Additionally, a code Orange Air Quality Alert for the Kansas City
metropolitan area is in effect Wednesday from 9 AM CDT to 7 PM CDT.

Members of sensitive groups may experience health effects.

People and businesses are urged to avoid activities which lead to
ozone formation. These activities include refueling vehicles or
topping off when refueling idling vehicles unnecessarily and using
gasoline powered lawn equipment. Positive activities include car
pooling, biking to work, delaying or combining errands, and using
water-based paints and cleaners.

When pollution levels are elevated, the Mid-America Regional Council
recommends that individuals consider limiting strenuous outdoor
physical activity to reduce the risk of adverse health effects.
People who may be especially sensitive to the effects of elevated
levels of pollutants include the very young and those with
preexisting respiratory problems such as asthma or heart disease.
Those with symptoms should consider consulting their personal
physician.

For further information, please see the Mid-America Regional Council
air quality program website at http://www.airqkc.org.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 1 at 10:22AM MDT until September 3 at 8:00PM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON WEDNESDAY TO 8 PM MDT
THURSDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR EAST BEAVERHEAD...

.Strong southwest winds will develop Wednesday as a cold front tracks
eastward and stalls along the Continental Divide. Winds will peak
each afternoon and early evening. Winds will remain elevated
Wednesday night, especially across midslopes and ridgetops, with poor
humidity recoveries.

The National Weather Service in Missoula MT has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 111.

* TIMING...From noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 20 to 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Make and maintain your go kit. Is it ready to go? Are there any
materials you need to refresh? Visit ready.gov/kit.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.
